record.original_question: Given a differentiable manifold M, determine whether M admits an almost complex structure.

evidence.quote: Almost complex structure in a manifold M

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth (differentiable) manifold. An almost complex structure on $M$ is a smooth $(1,1)$-tensor field $J$ on $M$, i.e. a smooth bundle endomorphism $J : TM \to TM$ of the tangent bundle, satisfying $J^2 = -\mathrm{id}_{TM}$ at every point. Equivalently, it is a reduction of the structure group of the tangent bundle from $GL(2n,\mathbb{R})$ to $GL(n,\mathbb{C})$ (which forces $\dim M = 2n$).

Problem: Find effective necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of the smooth/topological invariants of $M$, that determine whether a given differentiable manifold $M$ admits an almost complex structure. In particular, give a complete classification of those smooth manifolds $M$ which carry an almost complex structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Necessary conditions are classical: $M$ must be even-dimensional, orientable, and (in the compact case) its odd-dimensional integral Stiefel–Whitney classes must vanish, with further constraints coming from Chern/Pontryagin class congruences and obstruction theory. Existence is fully understood in low dimensions (e.g. dimension 2 and 4 via Wu's theorem) and for many specific families (spheres: only $S^2$ and $S^6$; certain homogeneous spaces, hyperbolic manifolds, homotopy $\mathbb{C}P^n$'s have been classified in recent works), but no single closed-form criterion is known for arbitrary smooth manifolds in higher dimensions. Hence the general classification problem is regarded as partially solved.
